correctness.rationale: For every finite graph and arbitrary marked diagonal, R reflexivises to the incidence order and the published finite duality applies. A nonreflexive edge-point belongs to an archival upset iff both endpoints do, forcing vertex membership to be constant on the connected components of the nonreflexive-edge subgraph. Each reflexive edge-point is independently optional only when both endpoint components are absent. This gives an inclusion-preserving bijection of archival upsets to upsets of the contracted quotient incidence poset, hence the order-dual congruence lattice is isomorphic to its downsets. Choosing absent quotient vertices gives the displayed exact induced-edge sum. Vertex loops are vacuous in the archival condition. All 761 edge-marked labeled graph cases up to four vertices passed direct archival enumeration; separate explicit finite-algebra compatible-element tests passed for four small graph families, including all vertex loop marks for two three-vertex cases.

originality.rationale: The new assertion is a graph-incidence contraction model for the entire congruence lattice, and its exact marked-graph count—not the general temporal-Esakia duality or the graph induced-edge polynomial itself. The full arXiv:2505.08014v2 and journal HTML were inspected in the sections on transits, archivalness, congruences and finite frames; these supply a general correspondence, but no marked incidence-graph quotient or cardinality formula. Independent published comparisons returned an incidence-poset homotopy theorem (different invariant) and unrelated chain-operator enumerations; no dominating claim was located. The 2024 Alvarez thesis abstract describes the general duality without an incidence-graph result, but its full text was not accessed, leaving a stated residual risk.
residual_risks: The older author thesis contains more material than its accessible abstract; its complete text was not compared and could contain an equivalent example.
Unindexed algebraic-logic or graph-poset research may independently contain the contracted-incidence congruence presentation.
Published general congruence/archival duality is expressly acknowledged as a major premise and is not newly proved.

value.rationale: The class comes canonically from incidence posets and temporal modal semantics rather than an arbitrary enumeration slice. The full congruence-lattice isomorphism describes all quotients and recovers the graph-derived simplicity criterion, and the induced-edge sum computes a natural all-markings invariant. It pinpoints the precise structural effect of missing edge loops: component contraction, while graph vertex loops are irrelevant. The result is stronger than a list of small counts and applies to every finite simple input graph.
